summary: Working with the team on the deployment software that installs, updates and keeps Honeywell's edge Kubernetes platform running, on appliances that ship fully offline or cloud-connected depending on what the customer picks.
description: Part of the team that cut update install time by 32.5% (about 90 to 61 minutes on a 44-package test run). The slow part wasn't any single package. It was a fixed wait after every install sequence while the datastore settled. That wait protects a real write limit, so we shrank it instead of removing it: 13 sequences became 9, the wait went from 120s to 60s, and tarball extraction moved to parallel pigz.

Worked on EdgeOrchestrator, the Go service on each appliance that drives installs and upgrades through Ansible, over MicroK8s, Ceph and Pacemaker. Playbooks run with an argument array so nothing reaches a shell, and a marker file stops a crashed self-update from being reported as a success.

Helped track down why some idle appliances kept wedging while an identical one stayed healthy. A hard stop of MicroK8s left network addresses unreleased until the pool ran out, and the platform's own watchdog restarted things in a way that triggered it again. We pre-cached the registry image, switched its rollout strategy, and added a circuit breaker that stops automatic restarts after more than 5 in a rolling 24 hours.

Collaborated on ForgeLinkLite, a cross-platform Go agent that enrolls devices with Azure Device Provisioning Service and keeps them connected to IoT Hub (certificate auth, AMQP over WebSocket). It has a KeePass-backed credential vault and active/passive failover.

summary: Built services across ForgeML's 8-microservice MLOps platform, running across 10+ tenant workspaces, and the pipeline that migrates SkySpark automation rules into Forge and translates them with a tuned model.
description: Built the deployment path that sends a model to Databricks Serving, AKS or edge devices through one API. Each target's config is validated at the boundary, and status is tracked by two separate async loops (endpoint status every 30 seconds, liveness every 5 minutes), so one failing doesn't stop the other.

Put model registration behind five security scanners (Coverity, Black Duck, Twistlock, ModelScan and an AST parser) using one shared interface. Adding a sixth means a new class, not another if-statement.

Fine-tuned Gemini on Vertex AI to translate SkySpark's Axon rules into Honeywell's Forge DSL, and built the versioned prompt store and tuning-job tracking around it. A translation only counted as correct if it gave the same results as the original rule, and domain experts reviewed the output. About 90% of translations passed.

Wrote the async Event Hub processor: events are read in real time, handed to one of three parsers, and written to PostgreSQL and Unity Catalog at the same time. Checkpoints are saved only after a successful write, and writes are upserts, so replaying after a crash overwrites rows instead of duplicating them.

Shipped the service that migrates SkySpark building-automation rules into Forge: SCRAM login, parsing SkySpark's Zinc and Trio formats, and parallel writes to PostgreSQL and Unity Catalog that roughly halved write time.
Wrote the Behave acceptance suite (50+ scenarios across six workflow areas, run in parallel per tenant) and the Locust load tests, from onboarding through deployment.

summary: Worked on the Databricks pipelines behind field service analytics, and the agent, memory and guardrail layers behind the Maintenance Assist chatbot.
description: Contributed to 15+ PySpark pipelines on Databricks that pull from 12+ source systems (SQL Server, Salesforce, SharePoint and field-service databases) into Delta Lake, loading only new data using timestamp watermarks.

Built a Spark Structured Streaming pipeline for PDFs landing in Blob Storage. It keeps revision history with a Delta MERGE per micro-batch (SCD Type 2), notices files deleted at the source, and turns on Change Data Feed so the downstream vectorization job reads only changed rows.
Wrote the SQL behind field service analytics (resolution trends by week, month and quarter, contract and maintenance metrics, NPS) that feeds the customer-facing DSP dashboard.
On the Maintenance Assist chatbot, worked on the agent executor (tool selection, chat history, summarization). A YAML config lets each tenant run its own LLM, tools and prompts without a code change.

Helped build guardrails that check input and output in parallel with the LLM call and cancel a response mid-stream, usually within a few tokens, if something breaks policy. The SSE streaming layer was built to support 100+ concurrent sessions.
Collaborated on a PGVector-backed chat memory that retrieves earlier turns by max inner product similarity rather than just recency.

Worked on vectorizing tens of thousands of knowledge-base articles and service cases, and contributed to the evaluation harness that scores chatbot answers with Azure OpenAI as the judge across 1,000+ question-answer pairs.
